fatal_errors: The room-temperature-only design cannot test the target's central cryogenic inertial-dulling or high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier mechanisms.

The proposed bulk tensile specimens do not reproduce the orientation-controlled single-crystal compression experiment needed to isolate critical resolved shear stress and dislocation-glide resistance.

Short-range ordering is introduced as a primary mediator without supporting evidence, while the target instead establishes MSAD-based lattice distortion and composition-specific dynamic solute pinning.
XRD peak broadening and conventional TEM alone do not provide an unambiguous quantitative measure of atomic-scale local distortion or short-range order.
explanation: The hypothesis captures one important part of the target: composition-dependent local lattice distortion can alter dislocation resistance and strength across Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni subsets. It also supplies a controlled compositional comparison and a nominally falsifiable correlation test. However, it remains generic and focuses on room-temperature yield strength, work hardening, and ductility rather than temperature-dependent single-crystal CRSS. It misses the target's two distinctive regimes—phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling below about 60–77 K and Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell-type dynamic pinning at elevated temperature—as well as strain-rate jumps, activation volumes, serrated flow, MSAD calculations, and the Suzuki-segregation TEM test. Predictions are qualitative and do not recover the Cr/MSAD strength trend, Mn+Fe dependence of the PL increment, or the observed temperature ranges. No prior evidence is cited, and the proposed structural measurements are not sufficiently specific to validate the claimed mediator.
